Staff were unaware of the care home's falls prevention policy. | Staff failed to correctly record falls and escalate incidents to senior staff. | The monthly falls log was not completed daily, leading to missed trends. | Observation forms were inaccurate due to staff completing them without seeing the patient. | Staff signed for observations while performing other tasks. | Documentation was not completed contemporaneously. | The home's policy treated the first fall as an isolated incident without further action. | The home's policy only escalated incidents to the falls team after three falls.
The unusual road layout at the junction may mislead pedestrians and motorists. | The proximity of a new school may increase pedestrian risks at the junction.
There are significant delays in the timely despatch and arrival of ambulance crews in response to 999 calls. | There are persistent vacancies for paramedic personnel.

Prison Service Instruction 64/2011 regarding daily medical reviews for prisoners under continuous observation is impracticable to implement. | Staff failed to attempt compliance with medical review requirements despite recognising the impracticability of the instruction. | National guidance is required to address the widespread inability to comply with daily medical reviews for prisoners under observation. | The ACCT procedure lacks a requirement for case managers to review recent observations prior to conducting reviews.

Inconsistent commissioning of mental health services creates unequal access to support for residents across Greater Manchester. | The Trafford Home Based Treatment Team lacks a mechanism to accept urgent GP referrals outside of standard office hours. | A lack of out-of-hours emergency GP referral pathways in Trafford necessitates reliance on A&E assessments.

The Transfer of Care Form was not completed by the examining doctor. | The Transfer of Care Form contained inaccurate clinical information. | The Transfer of Care Form was not provided to escorting officers for immediate return to custody.

There are no written protocols or pathways for the treatment of aortic aneurysms in Greater Manchester or the North West. | The absence of documented pathways prevents efficient and expedient referrals to appropriate surgical teams. | Inaccurate hospital naming during referrals can impede the transfer of patients requiring urgent care. | A lack of clear, unequivocal direction for referrals poses a risk of future patient deaths.

The discharge system for communicating patient information between hospitals and crisis teams was not robust. | The failure to provide immediate notification of discharge left a high-risk patient without necessary support. | Discharge procedures failed to account for the specific risks associated with a patient's home environment.
The clinical assessment of chest pain was insufficient to rule out myocardial infarction. | The results of blood tests showing raised troponin levels were not reviewed prior to discharge.
The suction excavator control panel was faulty due to joystick wear and tear. | The excavator could undergo involuntary downward movement when the control panel was detached.
The distance between the touchline and the clubhouse was less than the F.A. recommended guidelines. | The referee failed to take action regarding the breach of F.A. guidelines.

Communication failures between clinicians and hospital Trusts caused delays in patient transfer and clinical reviews. | Inadequate communication regarding patient instructions led to confusion among nursing staff regarding medication and nil by mouth status. | Consultant instructions were not consistently followed or communicated back when cancelled. | Standard ward placement failed to protect a patient with an unstable neck fracture from falling. | Inadequate staffing or monitoring protocols failed to prevent a patient from attempting to mobilise unassisted. | The hospital lacked immediate access to appropriate Balkan beam traction equipment. | Inadequate staff training resulted in the inability to locate necessary medical equipment. | The hospital lacked a safe and effective procedure for performing CT scans on patients in traction without releasing weights.

The laboratory failed to notify clinicians when the analyser malfunctioned. | No contingency plans were in place to ensure test analysis before patient discharge. | The electronic record system lacks a mechanism to alert clinicians when results are ready. | The availability of bedside ketone testing within the Trust was unconfirmed.

The site manager and designated first aider was not present on site at the time of the accident. | No workers remaining on site were trained in first aid. | Workers on site did not know how to contact emergency services.

Information sharing between relevant parties was inadequate. | Prison staff received insufficient guidance on providing appropriate support for potential victims of abuse. | Non-healthcare staff inappropriately relied on the deceased's presentation and views without further investigation.

Staff failed to identify or properly assess the risk of suicide and self-harm in newly arrived prisoners. | Healthcare staff did not participate fully in the health screen at reception or the first review of the ACCT. | Healthcare staff failed to carry out full and adequate risk assessments of suicide and self-harm during prisoner assessments. | There is a lack of a formal risk assessment tool for assessing suicide and self-harm.
The wearing of personal flotation devices on fishing vessel decks is not mandatory.

Clinicians should not presume the best case scenario when assessing patients who present in an inconsistent manner. | The assessment process lacks a formal check to ensure consistency in clinical treatment decisions. | The Trust lacks an adequate protocol for managing patients who appear to have capacity but decline care despite evidence of deterioration. | Clinicians should record specific concerns regarding patients who have capacity but remain at risk of self-harm. | Clinicians should consider sharing concerns about a patient's deteriorating condition with family and friends, subject to confidentiality rules. | Clinical notes and records lack sufficient justification for discharge decisions when previous assessments indicated a need for admission. | The Serious Incident Report was incomplete and failed to include formal interviews with relevant clinicians.

Whether proper consideration was given to balancing family contact restrictions against the acute needs and risks to the deceased. | Whether the needs and risks of vulnerable prospective defendants are adequately considered when setting bail conditions or restricting support.

The referral protocol for renal advice is limited and does not account for transplant patients. | There is insufficient availability of immunosuppressant medication at short notice. | New clinical protocols are not being effectively communicated or shared with all relevant staff.
Pentobarbital is subject to insufficient controls under the Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2001. | The lack of strict control over Schedule 3 drugs facilitates access to means of suicide.

The first aid equipment at the training site did not include an automated external defibrillator. | The training programme does not consistently offer automated external defibrillator training to all squadrons. | There were no communication checks between adult staff and cadets when the groups settled for sleep. | The radios available to the cadets were ineffective at the distance where staff were based. | The training instruction regarding communication checks for improvised camping is unclear. | Instructions fail to explicitly require instructors to ensure effective communication exists before cadets retire for the night.

The Mental Health Act assessment team left the property before adequate safeguards were implemented. | The Leicestershire Partnership Trust failed to communicate the availability of an available bed. | The local Trust failed to provide a facility for the reception of patients in cases of special urgency. | The statutory requirement to provide advice on arrangements for patients in cases of special urgency was not met.

The emergency medical despatcher incorrectly selected the protocol for a sick person instead of an unconscious person. | The London Ambulance Service failed to assign a red priority categorisation to a call regarding an unconscious patient. | There is a recurring failure in the handling of calls involving unconscious patients by the London Ambulance Service.

The Prison and Probation Service failed to communicate the actual release date to the prison in a timely manner. | Prisoners undergoing detoxification were not adequately informed of their actual release dates.

The Sheppey Road Bridge lacks a hard shoulder or safety lane for stationary vehicles. | There is a pattern of rear-end collisions involving stationary vehicles on the bridge. | Bridge geometry restricts forward visibility for drivers. | High vehicle speeds on the bridge impact overall safety. | The current 70 mph speed limit fails to mitigate identified safety risks.

Fluid balance charts were incomplete, rendering them an ineffective diagnostic tool. | An agency nurse failed to correctly calculate NEWS scores and failed to escalate the patient's deteriorating condition. | The Trust lacked a sufficiently rigorous system for monitoring the training and competence of agency staff.

Raised NEWS scores were not reported to ward doctors or the critical care outreach team. | National Early Warning Score assessments were inaccurate. | Clinical observations were not increased in frequency during periods of patient deterioration. | The nurse in charge failed to direct more frequent observations during clinical decline. | Clinical observations were recorded at incorrect times following a loss of consciousness. | There has been a repeated failure within the trust to use the NEWS tool properly.

The GP practice failed to implement systems to ensure patients receive appropriate medical reviews before repeat prescriptions are issued. | Patients prescribed citalopram were not being reviewed by a doctor at the required intervals of every three to six months.

The junction of Dover Road and Buckingham Avenue presents a risk of collisions between turning motor vehicles and cyclists. | Current cycle lane markings on Dover Road may encourage cyclists to position themselves in the blind spot of turning vehicles. | The sharing of the Dover Road carriageway between bicycles and motor vehicles may place cyclists at risk. | The existing road layout and cycle lane positioning may fail to ensure the safety of cyclists at junctions.

The care home failed to adequately monitor the resident to prevent unobserved departures. | The care home lacked a system to ensure clients were re-assessed when safeguarding orders expired. | The absence of CCTV at the care home entrances hampered the police investigation.

The deceased's mental capacity had not been assessed. | The care plan was incomplete, unsigned, undated and never reviewed. | No referrals were made to the Falls Team or Derbyshire Community Health regarding bed rails. | Responsibility for initial bed rails assessments was unclear. | The auditing process was insufficiently robust to identify care omissions. | A previous fall was not handed over, recorded or reported. | Staff responsibilities regarding incident reporting were unclear. | A staff member responsible for record making lacked sufficient literacy skills.

Staff lacked training in the appropriate use of 999 or 111 emergency services. | Staff were unable to arrange GP attendance for residents without permanent local registration. | The quality of resident observations was insufficient to identify basic clinical needs. | Staff failed to utilise visiting doctors to assess unwell residents. | Food and hydration records were not maintained. | Care records for residents were insufficient and improper. | Handover procedures during shift changes were not full or effective. | Out of Hours doctors lacked training in clinical record-keeping and vital sign assessment.

Paramedics failed to follow the Appropriate Care Pathway Policy by not performing clinical observations. | The absence of a radio protocol prevented the verification of critical PNC marker information between controllers and officers. | Police officers lacked sufficient training regarding the physiological effects of alcohol and the link between alcoholism and mental health. | Paramedics failed to recognise the medical implications of the individual's request for detoxification assistance.

The initial CT scan failed to identify the subdural haemorrhage. | The clinical examination was inadequate to identify the odontoid peg fracture. | There were missed opportunities for timely review by the trauma and orthopaedics team. | Systems for providing a cervical collar were inadequate. | Communication between the orthotics department and ward staff was poor.

Hospital staffing levels were insufficient during the patient's stay. | The procedure for escalating staff shortages was not properly implemented. | Nursing notes were not read or reviewed correctly by clinical staff. | The Emergency Department computerised system is incompatible with the wider hospital system. | Staff lacked sufficient training regarding the administration of cyclizine. | Clinical staff lacked a clear understanding of the required response to cardiac arrest. | Staff lacked adequate training in the dosage and delivery methods of certain prescribed drugs. | Hospital records contained inaccurate next-of-kin information.
The wearing of personal flotation devices on fishing vessel decks is not mandatory. | Legislation is required to make the wearing of personal flotation devices compulsory on working decks.
The appropriateness of implementing deterrent measures to the viaduct walls.

The lack of guard rails allows pedestrians to cross the road outside the designated crossing area. | The 90-degree bend creates a pinch point that complicates vehicle manoeuvres. | Vehicle blind spots and the building line restrict the driver's view of pedestrians at the junction. | The pedestrian crossing phase may not provide sufficient time for all pedestrians to cross the road safely.

The decision to downgrade patient supervision levels was not documented. | Bed rails were inappropriately raised, contributing to the patient's fatal fall. | The hospital failed to ensure patients were discharged with necessary oral pain relief. | Essential medical documentation, including the 'Do Not Resuscitate' form, was not transferred to the nursing home. | The Trust's internal investigation into the incident was unsatisfactory. | The Trust failed to cooperate adequately with police investigations.

The Clexane prescription did not follow the Derriford Protocol. | Pharmacy reviews failed to identify the incorrect Clexane dosage. | Inadequate weighing equipment for certain patients prevents accurate weight monitoring. | Failure to monitor weight changes led to inappropriate weight-dependent medication dosing.
The Hull Combined Court Centre lacked a defibrillator at the material time. | Public buildings such as court complexes lack essential defibrillation apparatus.

Nursing staff lacked sufficient room or resources to prevent patients from waiting in corridors. | No permanent medically qualified staff were stationed in the waiting area. | Emergency department waiting times frequently exceeded the national four-hour target.

Resource-based constraints in end-of-life care provision at HMP YOI Portland delayed the transfer to palliative care. | Healthcare staff lack formal guidance or training regarding the assessment of restraints and compassionate release. | Healthcare staff lack the necessary training to assess prisoner risks of re-offending or escape. | A lack of formal guidance may cause delays in effecting transfers or compassionate releases for terminally ill prisoners.

The purpose and training of the school's pastoral team were unclear. | The school's pastoral system was not sufficiently robust or structured to manage the student's needs. | It was unclear whether the student was informed of her rescheduled counselling appointment.

A lack of communication existed between the general practitioner and the podiatrist during the patient's consultation. | Clear guidance is required to determine which general practitioner is responsible for making secondary care referrals. | Administrative failures resulted in the failure to dispatch a necessary referral letter to secondary care providers. | The robustness of instructions to administrative staff regarding urgent referrals needs to be reviewed.

Manufacturer guidance for insulin pumps fails to adequately highlight the dangers of misuse and the potential consequences of incorrect cartridge insertion. | Diabetes patient education does not sufficiently emphasise the life-threatening risks associated with failing to manage a hyperglycaemic state.

Drivers do not expect to encounter stationary vehicles in a running lane. | High traffic speeds reduce the opportunity for evasive action. | High traffic volumes increase the number of people at risk from stationary vehicles. | Occupants of stationary vehicles have limited options to escape the carriageway. | Certain motorway stretches are unsuitable for use as smart motorways due to adjacent hazards.

A junior doctor failed to review a patient despite a significant increase in their NEWS score. | Clinical staff failed to recognise acute deterioration, potentially attributing physiological symptoms to patient anxiety. | Inconsistency existed between the use of NEWS forms and the governing MEWS escalation policy. | Nursing staff may feel reluctant to escalate concerns to senior doctors when junior doctors fail to act. | The lack of an automated electronic NEWS system may have contributed to clinical difficulties.
The therapeutic environment at the hospital was suboptimal. | The hospital failed to provide alternative therapeutic interventions when group therapy was declined.
Staff failed to ask the deceased if he was experiencing suicidal ideas or plans during clinical contact. | The care co-ordinator failed to record the concerns raised by the deceased's daughter.

The hospital policy failed to require constant visual observation of patients following the removal of a central venous catheter. | The hospital's quick reference guide allowed for intervals between dressing inspections that could permit fatal blood loss. | There is a lack of national guidelines and protocols regarding the removal of temporary central venous catheters for haemodialysis. | The electronic medical record system allowed staff to manually alter the author time of clinical notes. | The electronic system failed to provide unequivocal clarity by not recording both the time of an action and the time of the note.

The Trust failed to keep a patient at high risk of self-harm within eyesight as required by policy. | Patients frequently leave the accident and emergency department prior to receiving a psychiatric assessment. | Nursing staff lacked awareness of their legal powers to detain patients under the Mental Health Act. | The hospital failed to classify the incident as a serious incident for investigation.

The current position of the pedestrian crossing is unsafe. | The footpath by the mini roundabout lacks adequate pedestrian barriers. | The junction layout requires excessive attention from both drivers and pedestrians.
The 111 service failed to meet the mandated maximum waiting time for appointments. | The 111 system lacked a facility to effectively communicate clinical requirements between staff members.

Omnipaque doses exceeding manufacturer guidelines are frequently administered to interventional radiology patients. | The administration of hypertonic solutions through central lines may pose risks of toxicity to patients.

The Unable to Make Contact Protocol is insufficiently clear regarding when to request a police welfare check for high-risk patients. | The Protocol does not specify mandatory circumstances for requesting a welfare check, such as elapsed time or number of failed contact attempts. | The Trust failed to ensure that all staff, including shift co-ordinators, were adequately trained on the updated contact Protocol.

The Clinical Advisor failed to recognise critical red flags indicating the seriousness of the patient's condition. | The Clinical Advisor provided inappropriate advice that failed to safeguard the patient against the risk of deterioration. | The Trust failed to meet its target for auditing Clinical Advisor calls. | The lack of regular audits resulted in the absence of a safety net to identify potential risks or training needs. | The Trust lacked a structured response to actioning deficiencies identified during audits.
The gym failed to enforce the use of the treadmill emergency stop cord during user inductions.

The Mental Health Crisis Team failed to conduct a face-to-face assessment despite a GP referral. | The clinical determination by the Mental Health Crisis Team was made without sufficient inquiry. | The Mental Health Crisis Team overrode a GP's request for a mental health assessment without adequate justification. | NICE guidelines regarding antidepressant use may be applied too rigidly by mental health services.

Pulse oximeter alarm settings are routinely set at a fixed percentage rather than reflecting individual patient baselines. | The failure to account for a patient's normal oxygen saturation levels when setting alarms presents a potential risk to patient safety.

Carers facilitated smoking despite the significant risk of fire to the deceased and his neighbours. | Carers lacked training to assess whether the home environment or appliances posed a fire hazard. | Smoke detectors were insufficient to alert emergency services or allow the deceased to take evasive action.

The requirement to review radiology images before accepting the patient caused an unreasonable delay in transfer. | The request to escalate the clinical decision to a consultant was inappropriately declined. | The delay in accepting the patient for transfer reduced the opportunity for life-saving surgery.

The road surface at Stangrah Farm was in poor condition with unrectified potholes. | The road surface adhesion at the location was below the required standard. | A chevron warning sign was missing due to previous accident damage.

Denbighshire Social Services provided insufficient input to CAMHS safety plans, leaving carers with incomplete information to ensure young person safety. | Delays in scheduling professionals' meetings resulted in a failure to provide a prompt response to a crisis. | The decision to close the case without further assessment prevented necessary support from being provided to the deceased and her family. | A lack of senior staff review of case closure decisions may have prevented appropriate interventions.
The road markings in Coach Lane, Brading, are inadequate for ensuring road safety. | The absence of double yellow lines at the junction allows parked vehicles to obstruct visibility.

No action was taken by Next Stage following the initial disclosure of a medication overdose. | The Community Mental Health Team failed to respond to or action a message regarding a medication overdose. | Next Stage failed to follow up on an unreturned message left for the Community Mental Health Team. | Staff at Next Stage had not received updated training for managing medication overdose disclosures due to workload pressures. | Existing policies and procedures for managing medication overdose disclosures at Next Stage require review.

No formal mental capacity assessment or DoLS authorisation was undertaken in the community. | The hospital failed to recognise the patient's lack of mental capacity upon admission. | The hospital failed to request or review the patient's community care plan and SALT assessment. | Carers and the care co-ordinator failed to provide essential clinical information to the hospital.

A receptionist with no medical training performed patient streaming without conducting medical observations. | The streaming model caused significant delays in patients being seen by qualified healthcare professionals. | There are concerns regarding the required level of qualification for assessing patients within the streaming model. | The use of contracted services for urgent care requires scrutiny regarding patient safety. | Discrepancies in patient assessment based on mode of transport may incentivise inappropriate use of ambulance services.
Staff lacked specific, prescribed training on how to carry out and record resident observations.

The flowchart for responding to domestic abuse is vague and assesses depression risk rather than abuse risk. | The surgery lacks a specific domestic abuse questionnaire to assist in recognising signs of abuse. | There is no standardised procedure for GPs to respond to domestic abuse concerns. | No method exists for staff to recognise when a patient's call requires immediate escalation.
A robust and comprehensive action plan with timescales has not been implemented following the serious incident investigation.

Staff were not provided with sufficient training during the implementation of the new IT system. | The introduction of a new IT system resulted in the premature closure of patient access plans. | Failures in IT system implementation led to a lack of necessary clinical reviews for patients.

Insufficient safeguards exist for trauma patients placed on non-trauma wards. | System checks failed to ensure appropriate VTE prophylaxis for outlying patients. | Electronic Patient Record alerts are not being seen or acted upon by staff. | The Electronic Patient Record alert system fails to trigger if clinicians do not exit the patient record.
The pedestrian path lacked sufficient signage and lighting to indicate its status. | The site cabin placement created confusion regarding the accessibility of the path.

The system for delivering radiologist reports to the Emergency Department is unreliable and fails to provide effective safety netting. | The method of delivering paper reports to the Emergency Department is flawed and prone to failure. | There is no coding system to make radiologist reports identifying injuries easily identifiable for prioritisation. | The lack of a prioritisation system causes unnecessary delays in reviewing critical reports within the Emergency Department.

Inadequate monitoring of INR levels in a patient with dementia. | Lack of certainty regarding whether the patient was receiving prescribed Warfarin. | Inadequate communication between the INR Unit, the Care Home, and the GP surgery. | Failure to provide training to staff responsible for labelling blood samples. | Failure to notify the INR Unit of the patient's transfer to a new GP practice. | Failure to respond to correspondence regarding the lack of INR monitoring. | Failure to admit the patient to hospital despite concerns regarding a possible ischaemic leg.
Staff lacked a policy for reporting falls and contacting emergency services. | Staff training regarding the management of falls was inadequate.

The requested INR test was not performed following the consultant surgeon's review. | Warfarin was restarted based on an outdated INR reading without considering recent treatments. | There is a lack of clarity regarding protocols for reversing anticoagulation and restarting warfarin treatment.

The A66 lacks consistent dual carriageway status to manage high volumes of heavy goods vehicle traffic safely. | The variation between dual carriageway and winding single carriageway sections on the A66 poses a significant road safety risk.

Staff failed to open an ACCT despite the prisoner being visibly distressed. | The wing observation book lacked specific instructions regarding the delivery of support. | The prison lacked a defined process for offering support without opening an ACCT.

The GP surgery lacked an audit trail to confirm the sending of referrals via fax. | The surgery failed to consistently perform follow-up telephone calls to verify receipt of faxed referrals. | The referral process failed to ensure the Community Mental Health Team was notified of all patient referrals.

Nursing and medical notes failed to record family concerns regarding the patient's abdominal pain. | Medical records failed to document the attendance of out-of-hours doctors and specific medical reviews. | Handover processes between nursing and medical staff at shift changes were inadequate. | Multi-disciplinary team meeting minutes failed to record attendees, required actions, responsibilities, or timescales. | Clinical staff failed to communicate observed symptoms and family concerns to the reviewing medical team. | There were systemic failures in the quality of clinical documentation and staff training at the care centre.

Recommendations from the root cause analysis investigation may not have been implemented by the relevant teams. | Protective factors were not put in place for an individual who had indicated intent to self-harm and access to the means.
The adequacy of efforts to contact the patient following his non-compliance with follow-up care.

Information recorded in custody logs was not included in the Personal Escort Record. | Relevant information regarding a detainee's risk was not transmitted in writing to those responsible for subsequent detention.

The urgent CT pulmonary angiogram request was not acted upon. | The clinical team failed to follow up on the missing CT pulmonary angiogram procedure. | Radiology department staff incorrectly categorised the patient as an outpatient. | Reduced staffing levels during the Christmas period influenced the failure to process urgent requests.

There is no joint guidance for managing difficult airways when both anaesthetists and ENT surgeons are present. | Existing Difficult Airway Society guidelines do not cover the preferred mode of front of neck access for ENT surgeons.

Staffing levels during weekends and bank holidays are insufficient. | Advanced nurse practitioners are being used to replace junior and registrar level doctors. | The roles of ANNP and SANNP regarding medical versus nursing capacity are unclear. | Observations for children in NICU are not recorded seamlessly or easily viewable. | Nursing staff lack clear care plans and escalation markers to escalate concerns. | Nursing staff lack adequate training in recognising respiratory distress and PPHN. | Nursing staff lack the empowerment and leadership required to escalate clinical concerns. | There is no evidence of ongoing training for staff regarding PPHN and respiratory distress.
There were no arrangements in place to obtain a radiologist's opinion for x-rays during the early hours of the morning.

Tree foliage obstructed the street lamp, creating a large shadow across the road and pedestrian crossing. | The painted 'SLOW' road marking has faded and may be difficult for motorists to see. | The speed cushion allows vehicles to straddle it without reducing speed. | The speed cushion is beginning to disintegrate.

Delays in communicating consultant assessment summaries to GPs put vulnerable patients at risk. | Incompatible IT systems between the Mental Health Trust and GPs cause delays in information sharing. | The Mental Health team failed to return a call regarding concerns about a patient's wellbeing. | Staff are not accurately recording information or arranging necessary follow-up actions.

The emergency response procedures were not sufficiently efficient or effective. | The disaster recovery plan failed to ensure the immediate contact of emergency services. | Procedures were inadequate to expedite the arrival of emergency services to the site.

The risk of an adverse reaction to Buscopan in patients with coronary artery disease is not widely known. | The Summary of Product Characteristics lacks specificity regarding cardiac insufficiency. | The Summary of Product Characteristics does not explicitly encompass patients with ischaemic heart disease. | The medical community requires notification regarding potential cardiovascular risks when using intravenous Buscopan.

Staffing levels were insufficient to ensure required safety checks were completed during periods of high demand. | Staff lacked the necessary knowledge to access an outside telephone line to contact emergency services.
There are no telephones at the level crossing. | No contact telephone number for Network Rail is displayed at the crossing. | There is a risk of repeat incidents at this location.
Quad bike riders are not required to wear crash helmets when driving on public roads. | There are no additional driving qualifications required to operate a quad bike.

CQC regulation of private medical companies provides false security regarding the scope of regulated activities. | The exemption for temporary arrangements leaves medical assistance at events entirely unregulated. | The title of ambulance technician is not protected or regulated. | Private medical training providers fail to verify the suitability of mentors for trainees.

The safety of the Millpond is a concern following three deaths in recent months. | Certain areas of the Millpond may require fencing. | Lighting at the Millpond may need improvement. | The adequacy of warning notices at the Millpond requires consideration. | The availability of flotation equipment at the Millpond requires consideration.

Monitoring of District Nurse compliance with delegated INR testing is not uniform across all Level 4 Accredited GP practices. | GP practice procedures fail to provide adequate checks to prevent unmonitored failures in delegated District Nurse tasks. | A risk exists of future deaths due to unmonitored over-anticoagulation following failure to perform delegated INR testing.
A national monitoring scheme for inexperienced consultant surgeons has not been formulated.

MRI scan results were not sent to the correct consultant. | The recommendation for a follow-up scan was not followed up. | The requested outpatient appointment was not arranged. | Ward Administrators were unaware of their responsibility to book follow-up appointments. | A systemic failure existed where follow-up appointments were not booked for many patients.

Required hourly nursing observations were not performed. | Nursing observations were not recorded in the medical notes. | Nursing record keeping was inadequate. | No attempts were made to ensure a doctor attended to review the patient following an elevated MEWS score. | No follow-up review was arranged after the implementation of a fluid challenge. | Doctors failed to maintain complete and accurate medical records during clinical reviews. | The incident investigation failed to include identified failures in nursing and medical care.
The suitability of pedestrian railings between Paignton railway station and bus station requires review to reduce vehicular collisions.

Individuals with co-occurring addiction and mental health difficulties may fall between service gaps. | A lack of coordination exists when mental health services and alcohol treatment services fail to provide integrated care. | Insufficient information sharing occurs between agencies involved in providing support services. | No single agency is identified as the lead for communication purposes.

The lack of a formal risk assessment tool for Deep Vein Thrombosis is inadequate. | There is no interim risk assessment tool in place during pathway changes. | LMWH prophylaxis for patients with lower limb immobilisation is not applied uniformly across Trusts. | The hospital lacks a model to facilitate discussions regarding the risks and benefits of prophylaxis. | The absence of national guidance creates a postcode lottery regarding the provision of prophylaxis.

Airedale Hospital failed to provide discharge papers for a patient following a neurological assessment. | Airedale Hospital failed to include written recommendations for neurological observations in the patient's discharge instructions. | Riverview Nursing Home failed to refer the patient to hospital promptly following the onset of seizures.

The risk assessment document failed to include a completed assessment of suicide risk. | Staff frequently fail to complete the suicide risk section of risk assessment documentation. | Risk assessments are being extrapolated from actions taken rather than being explicitly recorded.

The common practice of operatives working in close proximity to reversing trucks poses a significant risk. | The requirement for ground workers to issue tickets to drivers necessitates dangerous proximity to moving vehicles. | There is a lack of technological systems to replace manual ticketing processes during muck away operations.

Prison Service Instruction 64/2011 fails to describe symptoms of undiagnosed mental illness as risk factors for suicide. | The Prison Service Instruction 64/2011 lacks specific inclusion of irrational behaviour and being out of touch with reality as suicide risk factors. | The absence of specific risk descriptors in PSI 64/2011 prevented the timely opening of an ACCT to monitor the prisoner.

Neurosurgical patients lack sufficient support from consultant physician colleagues. | Junior neurosurgical doctors are left to implement alcohol withdrawal regimens without adequate supervision. | The Trust's alcohol withdrawal protocol is difficult to understand. | Errors in medication prescribing occurred due to unclear clinical protocols.
The safety of the Maplin N19KJ telescopic ladder is a matter of concern. | The origin of the accident ladder requires verification.
The interaction between verapamil and clarithromycin was not recognised at the time of prescription. | Not all doctors were aware of the BNF mobile app used to identify potential drug interactions.

General practitioners are not routinely invited to MARAC meetings. | Risks and safeguarding measures identified by MARAC were not communicated to the general practitioner. | The general practitioner was not informed of allegations of domestic abuse and coercive control. | The general practitioner was not made aware of significant stressors involving care proceedings.

The wooden access gate at Lower Farm Road provides insufficient deterrence against unauthorised entry to the railway line. | The wooden fence surrounding the access gate is of inadequate height to prevent access to the tracks. | The identified need to replace the wooden track access gate with more significant fencing has not been addressed.
Communication between the Trust and the GP regarding the risks of delayed pessary removal was inadequate. | Regular maintenance and hygiene procedures for the pessary were not sufficiently observed.

The water tank cover had not undergone maintenance for at least 19 years. | Severe deterioration of timber and corrosion of metal fixings occurred due to lack of maintenance. | RICS guidance does not require surveyors to refer to areas of a building not accessed. | Surveyors are not mandated to advise clients on the risks of not obtaining access for inspections.

The prison escort record is not checked on arrival to ensure all required risk assessments are included. | Healthcare staff failed to follow mandatory instructions for high-risk scores on the first night reception template. | Staff lacked clarity regarding the purpose and clinical significance of the first night reception template. | The GP failed to explore known suicidal triggers during the initial clinical assessment. | Healthcare staff failed to investigate the absence of a prisoner from a scheduled clinical screening. | The root cause analysis was not disclosed to the Coroner or relevant prison and healthcare management.

The NICE Head Injury Pathway failed to include Clopidogrel as a trigger for a CT scan despite the risk of increased bleeding. | The clinical pathway did not account for the increased risk of trauma-related bleeding in patients prescribed Clopidogrel.

Police staff lacked formal training regarding risk assessment and child mental health. | Staff demonstrated intentional disregard for Force policies and operational protocols. | The Force lacks set minimum staffing levels for divisional response and the OCB. | Senior leadership failed to take sufficient action to address persistently low staffing levels. | Decisions to withhold additional resources were not recorded with a rationale or contemporaneous minutes. | The Chief Inspector failed to communicate decisions regarding resource allocation to relevant personnel. | The Force failed to allocate the missing person report, resulting in the loss of the Golden Hour. | Multiple delays were placed on the incident log without recorded justification.
Helium is a toxic gas that is readily available for purchase on the high street or online.

Prison healthcare staff continued administering digoxin after hospital clinicians requested its discontinuation. | Communication failed between the hospital and the prison following the patient's discharge. | Discharge correspondence was not immediately available to or reviewed by prison healthcare staff. | There is a lack of electronic transfer of discharge summaries to prison healthcare facilities.
No support was provided regarding accommodation following the deceased's release from prison.

Care staff lacked adequate training regarding PEG feeding, mobility, and resident handling. | Management failed to review staff training or risk assessments following clinical incidents. | Incidents involving PEG feeding and vomiting were not recorded by the care home. | Management was unaware of significant clinical incidents due to poor internal reporting procedures. | Staff were not fully conversant with the controls for pausing PEG feeding during resident movement. | Essential medical equipment, such as bed remote controls, was non-functional due to lack of maintenance.

GP referrals for psychiatric assessment are not being seen by qualified psychiatrists. | Staff without appropriate qualifications are being used to compensate for a shortage of qualified doctors. | Mental health teams are failing to complete or document necessary risk assessments. | Inadequate documentation of risk assessments prevents effective communication of patient risks within clinical teams. | The lack of continuity in team-based care increases risks to patients.

The medical assessment process contains serious deficiencies regarding investigations into health conditions listed on the POLN3 form. | The process fails to ensure follow-up when a GP identifies a relevant consultant. | The POLN3 form does not allow drivers to explain the relevance of identified consultants. | The POLN3 form does not allow doctors to express general reservations regarding fitness to drive. | Inadequate medical assessments may permit unfit drivers to continue driving.
Prioritising student privacy over welfare concerns caused delays in attending the scene and reluctance to force entry. | The lack of timely intervention poses a risk of future student deaths.
